RACE FINDER

Browse the returns

Coverage, sources and methodology
Open House Clerk records ↗

Presidential state returns run from 1868 to 2024, congressional returns from 1976 to 2024, and selected governor returns from 1990 to 2025. The era controls list years with interactive data. Earlier cycles have gaps where no popular vote was held or the source has no tabulation. The House Clerk’s official archive has earlier federal records and midterms.

Pre-1976 presidential popular votes are adapted from The American Vote, State results in U.S. presidential elections, 1789–2024 (CC BY 4.0). This site groups candidates into party display categories and computes shares from the included votes. National electoral totals are checked against the National Archives.

Federal returns from 1976 onward are from MIT Election Data and Science Lab’s presidential, Senate and House datasets. See also the Federal Election Commission’s official compilation and Electoral College certificates.

Governor returns are available where covered by the Election Wrld archive, compiled from state offices and the Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder dataset. This archive covers major general elections. Primary and local results have separate coverage.

Percentages use the candidate votes included in the displayed tabulation. Fusion ballot lines are combined by candidate name. Vote totals may reflect different rounds across states, and close margins are descriptive. House colors summarize district results within each state. Presidential colors show statewide popular votes, including in states that split their electoral votes.

How comparisons work

Statewide swing is the change in the Democratic-minus-Republican share of all candidate votes shown. Third-party leaders still appear. Comparisons require a return in both years. For Senate, a state comparison can involve different seats, and only the regular race is compared.

House comparisons count top finishers by state. District boundaries and the number of seats can change, so the tool compares statewide delegations. Archive links open the underlying records.

How the outlook updates

Federal general election dates follow the statutory November schedule. Featured off-year dates link to the responsible state election office. The race tracker queries civicAPI for the selected election and refreshes more frequently around election day while this page is open. Candidate listings and unofficial results appear as the provider publishes them.

The connected polling feed uses surveys indexed to the selected cycle and, where applicable, state and office. Selected 2028 primary polls link directly to the pollsters. The archive and outlook have different coverage. The 2026 atlas remains available from the Returns tab.
